title: Leakage-Aware Content Refresh Opportunity Scoring
short_description: A predictive ranking and triage system that helps reviewers decide which content pages to inspect first. It uses 26 engineered features, temporal development windows, a held-out future month and leakage audits, comparing Logistic Regression with Random Forest under client-grouped validation. It improves ranking performance over a fixed baseline; it makes no causal claim about refreshing content.
detailed_description: A leakage-aware time-split ranking model for prioritizing content-refresh review, evaluated on a held-out future month.

facts.label: Problem
facts.text: Content teams have more pages worth investigating than they can review at once. The research question was whether March-only, non-label-derived search and engagement signals can rank content that later meets a predefined refresh-review condition in April.

facts.label: Approach
facts.text: A predictive ranking and triage system to support human review, not automated publishing. Development panels used January→February and February→March, with a held-out future test window of March→April.

facts.label: Methods
facts.text: 26 engineered features from search position, GA4 engagement and traffic-channel signals; leakage audits; Logistic Regression and Random Forest compared with client-grouped validation using Average Precision; a tiered review queue with reason codes.

facts.label: Outcome
facts.text: Random Forest outperformed a fixed Week-4 baseline on the held-out month (Precision@20 0.65 against 0.40; Average Precision 0.4838 against 0.3807). This shows improved ranking performance, not a causal effect of refreshing content.

home_visuals.note: Dashed line: the 23.74% positive-class base rate, the level a random ranking would reach. Higher is better.
